city.name: Athens
city.location_name: Argentinis Dimokratias Square — reference pin; not claimed to be the precise sensor point

pain.statement: Extreme urban heat produces uneven surface thermal exposure and unequal access to cooler public places.

verified_observation.value: 60°C exposed paving vs 30°C under tree shade
verified_observation.context: Surface temperature measurements reported for Argentinis Dimokratias Square during summer 2025; not air temperature.
verified_observation.cross_check_note: Municipal field update separately reports shaded/natural-material spots around 30°C and conventional surfaces over 50°C at several locations; it corroborates the scale of surface differences, not the exact same paired reading.

secondary_observation.context: Reported at Agia Irini Square after cool materials and targeted shading.

population_context.warning: 2021 census municipal population context only; not a count of people harmed by heat or an estimate of exposure.

programme_targets.status: programme targets, not verified completed outcomes

pain.affected_people_note: No defensible count for people specifically affected at the reference square was found in reviewed sources. Population is not substituted for an affected-person count.

technology.name: #CoolAthens
technology.details: Municipal heatwave information; cites an algorithm using two decades of historical weather and mortality data and updated temperature/thermal-discomfort maps.

technology.name: Cooling Havens
technology.status: municipal programme under implementation/planning as described on official site
technology.details: Water reuse, rain gardens, blue-green public spaces and IoT environmental monitoring; targets labelled as targets.

technology.name: Athens urban cooling interventions
technology.details: Thermal camera readings for shaded streets, cool surfaces, a microforest and a cooling garden.

playable_world.mechanics: Place three interventions on empty tiles near three heat hotspots. Win by covering all hotspots; using all modules without coverage is a loss. Scores are illustrative, not scientific predictions.
playable_world.ar: WebXR immersive-ar attempted only if browser support is detected; availability varies by device/browser.

evidence_register.name: Municipality of Athens — Cooling Havens
evidence_register.supports: Six intervention sites, water reuse, rain gardens, IoT sensors and stated targets for more than 8,000 m² infrastructure, up to 5°C local cooling and over 70% rainwater retention.

evidence_register.name: EU Covenant of Mayors — Athens Hits Refresh
evidence_register.supports: Summer 2025 field report: around 60°C exposed pavement vs 30°C tree shade at Argentinis Dimokratias Square; 4–6°C at Agia Irini.

evidence_register.name: NetZeroCities — Cooling Athens
evidence_register.supports: Separate programme publication reporting comparable site-level thermal findings.

evidence_register.name: Municipality of Athens — Local cooling measures
evidence_register.supports: Separate municipal statement: around 30°C in shaded/natural-material areas vs above 50°C on conventional surfaces at several sites; corroborates magnitude, not exact same paired measurement.

evidence_register.name: NTUA UWMH — Cooling Havens
evidence_register.supports: University research project timeline and the city’s impermeable surface challenge.

evidence_register.name: Municipality of Athens — #CoolAthens
evidence_register.supports: Official heat-risk information service, described algorithm using two decades of weather/mortality data and maps updated every 15 minutes.

evidence_register.name: ELSTAT — 2021 Census
evidence_register.supports: Official population census, Athens municipality permanent population.

evidence_register.name: CNI Greece — Athens municipality

social_pack.short_video_caption_en: 60°C on exposed pavement. 30°C under tree shade. Could you redesign one city block? Play ZION-030: three hotspots, three interventions, one mission. Based on Athens’ reported 2025 surface measurements. Game score is illustrative — the field evidence is real.
social_pack.x_en: Athens reported a surface-temperature gap: ~60°C on exposed paving vs ~30°C under tree shade. We turned the evidence into a playable 3D mission. Place trees, canopies and rain gardens. Can you cover all three hotspots?
social_pack.instagram_en: The heat is measurable. Shade changes the surface. Cooling tools already exist. Now it’s your turn to redesign the block. ZION-030 is live as a browser game; evidence and limits are documented in the field dossier.
social_pack.telegram_en: NEW EPISODE — THE SHADE PROTOCOL. Athens’ 2025 thermal-camera reporting showed exposed pavement around 60°C and ground under tree shade around 30°C. The city already uses heat-risk information and cooling interventions. We built a 3D mission where you place three interventions beside heat hotspots. This is a simulation, not an official city planning tool. Primary sources, programme targets and business assumptions are linked in the dossier.
hook_tests: A — Number: This pavement reached 60°C. Look what shade did.
B — Challenge: Three hotspots. Three interventions. Can you cool the block?
C — Mystery: ZION-9 points at empty pavement. A city appears — and you have 3 moves to fix it.
social_pack.publishing_status: drafts only; no social platforms have been auto-published
